meta.title: Carriage of passengers and goods
meta.summary: You will learn how the Rules require you to carry children, people in a truck's load body and bus passengers, and how to position, secure and mark a load so that it does not get in anyone's way or put anyone at risk.

p: A child in a car is far more vulnerable than an adult. The standard seat belt is designed for an adult's height, so during hard braking it can cross a child's neck or stomach. This is exactly why child restraints are needed.
The Rules prohibit carrying children under 12 unless there is a special child restraint or other means that allow the child to be belted in with the standard seat belt ⟦18⟧.
The rule is stricter for the front seat: a child under 12 may be carried there only in a special child restraint. A seat belt adapter is not enough for the front seat.
list: Back seat: a child seat (restraint) or another means for belting the child in with the standard seat belt
Front seat of any motor vehicle, including a truck cab: only a special child restraint
You must not carry a child in your arms, either in front or in the back. There is no exception for taxis
The text of the Rules sets the limit by age only (under 12). Height is not mentioned in para. 157: it only matters when choosing a restraint according to the manufacturer's instructions
From age 12, a child travels like an adult, but must always be belted in ⟦19⟧
lesson.tip: For the exam, remember this pair: “under 12” and “front seat: restraint only”.

p: Paragraph 156 lists the ways passengers must not be carried. The logic is simple: a person must be somewhere the vehicle's design protects and holds them.
A motorcycle or moped driver must themselves wear a fastened motorcycle helmet and must not take a passenger who is not wearing a fastened motorcycle helmet ⟦20⟧.
list: Outside the cab of a car, tractor or self-propelled machine; on a goods trailer; in a caravan trailer; in the load body of a goods motorcycle; and outside the seating positions on a motorcycle. Exception: the flatbed body of a truck or a box body
More people than the vehicle's technical specification provides for. The mass of the vehicle with people on board must not exceed the manufacturer's maximum authorised mass
An intoxicated passenger on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped
More people than there are seats fitted in a truck's load body
Children under 16 on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped

lesson.h: People in a truck's load body: who may carry them
p: Carrying people in a load body is a serious responsibility, so there are special requirements for the driver ⟦21⟧. The driver must be 25 years old, must hold category “C” and must have more than five years of driving experience specifically in that category. Overall experience driving a car does not count.
If, together with the passengers riding in the cab, there are more than 8 people in total, the driver needs categories “C” and “D”.

Buses have their own thresholds: subcategory “D1” (more than 8 but not more than 16 seats, not counting the driver) - from age 21, with at least three years of experience working as a driver, including at least one year on “C1”; category “D” - from age 23, with at least three years of experience, including at least one year on “D1” ⟦22⟧.
Vehicles with right-hand drive, or with special controls, including fully manual controls, must not be used as taxis ⟦23⟧.

lesson.h: Travelling with people in the load body
p: A flatbed body is fitted out under the Basic Provisions ⟦24⟧: seats are placed at a height of 0.3-0.5 m from the floor and at least 0.3 m below the top edge of the side, and seats along the rear or side must have sturdy backrests. For carrying children, the sides must be at least 0.8 m high from the floor.

Before setting off, the driver explains to passengers how to get in, get out and settle in the load body, and warns them: standing in the load body or sitting on the sides while the vehicle is moving is not allowed. The driver may move off only after making sure that the conditions for safe carriage have been met ⟦25⟧.
If the load body is not fitted out for people, only those who are escorting the load or travelling to collect it may ride in it. And only if they have a seat below the level of the sides ⟦26⟧.
The speed of a truck carrying people in the load body must not exceed 60 km/h ⟦27⟧. In built-up areas, a 50 km/h limit already applies to trucks anyway ⟦28⟧.
lesson.tip: You must not stand in the load body, even if you are driving slowly.

p: You may let people on or off only where stopping is not prohibited, and only after coming to a full stop. Move off only with the doors closed, and open them only after coming to a full stop ⟦29⟧.

Stopping is ceasing to move for up to 5 minutes, or longer if this is needed for boarding or alighting passengers, or for loading or unloading ⟦30⟧. So within the zone of sign 3.28 “No parking” you may drop off a passenger or unload the vehicle, but within the zone of sign 3.27 “No stopping” you may not.

The driver of a route vehicle lets passengers on and off only at a designated stop ⟦31⟧. For category M2 and M3 buses, the ban on stopping at route-vehicle stop areas and within 15 m of them does not apply ⟦32⟧.
The rules are strictest for organised groups of children, because a single bus carries many children at once ⟦33⟧.
list: A bus with at least two doors
An amber flashing beacon
The “Carriage of children” sign at the front and rear
A driver aged at least 25, holding the required category, with at least five years of experience working as a driver
No more children than there are seats
A convoy of two or more buses carrying children on roads outside built-up areas is escorted by special vehicles of the internal affairs bodies

p: A load is carried on vehicles designed for that purpose. On a bus, load and luggage are carried only in the luggage compartment ⟦34⟧.
The mass of the load and passengers, and the distribution of the load across the axles, must not exceed the manufacturer's figures ⟦35⟧. Overloading makes braking and handling worse.
The driver checks how the load is positioned, secured and covered, not only before the trip but also on the way ⟦36⟧. If the load has shifted or a strap has come loose, stop and fix it.
A load may be carried only if it meets all the conditions of para. 162:
list: Positioned and, if necessary, secured so that it does not endanger people or damage other people's property
Does not restrict the driver's view
Does not make the vehicle harder to control or affect its stability
Does not cover the headlights, lights, brake lights, direction indicators, retroreflectors, number plates or the country identification sign, and does not stop hand signals from being seen
Does not create avoidable inconvenience
lesson.tip: If the load's position cannot be corrected, you must not continue driving ⟦37⟧.

lesson.h: Size and mass include the load
p: Signs 3.11 “Weight limit”, 3.12 “Axle load limit”, 3.13 “Height limit” and 3.14 “Width limit” concern the vehicle's actual dimensions and mass together with the load. A vehicle that is 3.2 m high, with a load 3.8 m high, will not fit under a sign 3.13 marked “3.5 m”.
For sign 3.12, the load on each axle is checked, not the average. That is why a load is distributed across the axles in advance ⟦38⟧.
lesson.tip: Always count height, width and mass together with the load.

p: Other drivers can easily fail to notice a long or wide load. That is why it must be marked ⟦39⟧.

If a load extends more than 1 metre beyond the front or rear, or more than 40 centimetres beyond the side, measured from the outer edge of a position lamp, the “Oversized load” sign is fitted: a 400×400 mm panel with alternating red and white diagonal stripes on a retroreflective surface.
During hours of darkness and in poor visibility, a light is added: a white lamp or retroreflector at the front, and a red one at the back.

Vehicles longer than 20 m (including with one trailer) and road trains with two or more trailers are marked at the rear with the “Long vehicle” sign - a yellow rectangle with a red border (Basic Provisions).

Overweight, oversized and dangerous loads are carried under a special procedure set by the authorised transport authority ⟦40⟧. A vehicle carrying dangerous goods is marked at the front and rear with the “Dangerous goods” sign: an orange retroreflective rectangle 300×400 mm with a black border and markings showing the goods' hazardous properties (Basic Provisions, para. 9).
lesson.tip: Numbers for how far a load may extend: 1 m at the front or back, and 40 cm at the side. White light faces forward, red faces back.

keyFacts: Children under 12 are carried in a child restraint or with another means of belting them in with the standard seat belt ⟦1⟧
In the front seat, a child under 12 is carried only in a special child restraint ⟦2⟧
Children under 16 must not be carried on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped ⟦3⟧
People are carried in a load body by a driver aged 25 with category “C” and more than 5 years of experience in that category ⟦4⟧
Standing in the load body or sitting on the sides while moving is not allowed ⟦5⟧
A truck carrying people in the load body travels no faster than 60 km/h ⟦6⟧
Route vehicles let passengers on and off only at a designated stop ⟦7⟧
A bus for an organised group of children: at least 2 doors, an amber beacon, “Carriage of children” signs, a driver aged 25 or over with at least 5 years of experience ⟦8⟧
On a bus, luggage is carried only in the luggage compartment ⟦9⟧
A load that extends more than 1 m beyond the front or rear, or more than 40 cm beyond the side, is marked with the “Oversized load” sign ⟦10⟧
In the dark, a projecting load is marked with a white lamp or retroreflector at the front and a red one at the back ⟦11⟧
If the load cannot be positioned correctly on the spot, the driver must stop and not continue driving ⟦12⟧
mistakes: “You can hold a child in your arms on the back seat if it's not far to go.” Not allowed: a child under 12 needs a restraint or another means of belting them in ⟦13⟧.
“A 10-year-old can sit in the front with a belt adapter.” Not allowed: in the front, a child under 12 is carried only in a special child restraint ⟦14⟧.
“You can stand in the load body if you hold on to the side.” Not allowed: standing in the load body and sitting on the sides while moving are both prohibited ⟦15⟧.
“Any projecting load must be marked.” The sign is needed only when a load extends more than 1 m beyond the front or rear, or more than 40 cm beyond the side ⟦16⟧.
“If the load is securely fastened, it doesn't matter that it covers the number plate.” A load must not cover number plates, lights or retroreflectors ⟦17⟧.
“My vehicle is under 3.5 m, so I can pass under sign 3.13.” Signs 3.11-3.14 take into account the mass and dimensions together with the load.
